name: Directus
tools_source: https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/main/api/src/controllers/server.ts + services/server.ts (/server/info, /server/health), api/src/controllers/collections.ts (/collections), api/src/controllers/items.ts (/items/:collection), api/src/controllers/users.ts (/users/me); query parameters per https://docs.directus.io/reference/query.html
description: Self-hosted Directus reads: project and version info, instance health, the collections the token can see, the identity behind the static token, and items out of one collection. Read-only; the POST, PATCH and DELETE routes on the same /items, /collections, /users and /fields endpoints are deliberately absent, as is /server/setup.

tools.name: server_info
tools.description: Get the Directus project name, version and query limits for the instance this credential points at

tools.name: server_health
tools.description: Get the Directus instance health: overall status plus the per-service checks (database, cache, storage, email)

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List the Directus collections the static token is permitted to read, with their notes and display metadata

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Identify the Directus account the stored static token belongs to

tools.name: list_items
tools.description: Read items out of one Directus collection, optionally narrowed by a field list, a full-text search term or a sort order

collection.description: Collection name to read from. Directus system collections (directus_*) are rejected by the API on this route

limit.description: Max items to return (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

offset.description: Number of items to skip before returning results

sort.description: Comma-separated field names to sort by; prefix a name with '-' for descending

search.description: Full-text search term matched against the collection's string and text fields

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to return (Directus defaults to every field the token may read)

meta.description: Metadata to compute alongside the items: 'total_count', 'filter_count', or '*' for both

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, AND THE VAULT AGREES: the REST reference (https://docs.directus.io/reference/introduction.html) documents a static token as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', so {type: bearer, field: token} is unchanged. The vault entry (integrationTypeRegistry.directus) sends the identical header in testHeaders and its testEndpoint is base_url + /users/me, which is this spec's test block verbatim. Directus also accepts ?access_token= in the query string; the header form is used because it keeps the credential out of URLs and logs.

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: Directus is self-hosted, base_url comes from the credential ({fromCredential: 'base_url'}), and Directus Cloud instances each carry their own hostname, so there is no vendor-run host to shape-prove against. This spec is NOT SHAPE_PROVEN by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral Directus container, creates the admin user and a collection named 'quoxproof-live', and drives every tool against it.

CATEGORY: the scaffold wrote 'uncategorized', which is not one of the twelve values in use across this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management). Changed to 'files_knowledge', which is where the other headless CMS and structured-document platforms already sit (contentful, coda, pandadoc). The vault entry says 'documents', which is not a spec-directory value; 'files_knowledge' is its equivalent.

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH INSTANCE, BY CONSTRUCTION: server_info, server_health, list_collections and get_current_user need no resource at all and carry an empty _probe. list_items is the only tool that needs an existing resource, and it probes collection='quoxproof-live', the exact name the live provisioner creates; an empty collection answers with data: [] rather than an error.

RESPONSE ENVELOPE IS NOT UNIFORM, AND THE PICKS ENCODE THAT: /server/info, /collections, /items/:collection and /users/me all wrap their payload in {data} (controllers/server.ts sets payload = {data}, items.ts sets {meta, data}), so those picks are dotted through 'data'. /server/health is the ONE exception: services/server.ts returns the health object at the TOP LEVEL, so status/releaseId/serviceId/checks are picked unprefixed. It also answers with Content-Type application/health+json rather than application/json, which the runtime's resp.json() does not care about, and it returns HTTP 503 (not 200) when a dependency is down, which the runtime surfaces as an error rather than as health data.

TWO FIELDS ARE PRIVILEGE-DEPENDENT, AND THAT IS A MISSING KEY RATHER THAN A FAILURE: services/server.ts only populates info.version when the accountability carries a user, and /server/health returns the full {status, releaseId, serviceId, checks} object ONLY to an admin accountability, degrading to bare {status} for everyone else. A non-admin static token therefore yields null for release_id, service_id and checks. getPath is null-safe, so nothing throws; the live harness should record which of the two token classes it proved.

list_items CANNOT HAVE A FIELD-LEVEL PICK, SO IT HAS A TWO-KEY ALLOWLIST INSTEAD: every other tool here picks named fields, but the items in a Directus collection are USER-DEFINED, so no field list can be written in advance. The pick is therefore {meta, data}, which still acts as an allowlist against any future top-level envelope key, and truncate 2000 still caps every string inside the rows. The 'fields' input is the real lever for narrowing the payload, and it narrows it SERVER-side.

LIMIT CLAMP IS OURS AND SITS BELOW DIRECTUS'S OWN: QUERY_LIMIT_DEFAULT is 100 and QUERY_LIMIT_MAX defaults to -1 (unlimited), both readable from server_info's query_limit_default / query_limit_max. The 20/50 clamp therefore never asks for more than an instance will return, and the input description says the cap is this connector's rather than a Directus fact. /collections and /users/me take no limit, so neither carries one.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all five tools are GETs. The same controllers expose POST/PATCH/DELETE on /items/:collection, /collections, /users and /fields, plus POST /server/setup which creates the first admin. None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing a Directus instance.

ONE ROUTE IS ENV-GATED UPSTREAM: /server/health is only mounted when HEALTHCHECK_ENABLED is not false (controllers/server.ts), so server_health can 404 on an instance that has disabled it. That is a deployment choice, not a spec defect, and the live harness runs with the default.
